channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler: a third exploited zero-day joins CISA’s KEV list, and responders warn patching alone will not evict intruders
item.description: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution) and CVE-2026-88772 (a memory overflow on appliances with DTLS enabled), both CVSS v4 9.5, were exploited before fixes shipped, and CISA added both to its KEV catalog that day. On 4 October CISA added a third, CVE-2026-88779 (CVSS v4 8.7), a memory overflow on appliances configured for SAML that Citrix says it has seen used in targeted attacks causing denial of service; federal agencies must fix it by 7 October. watchTowr reproduced it as a crash-only bug and suspects attackers use it to knock appliances over and speed up exploitation of CVE-2026-88771; one researcher reported signs of code execution, but Citrix says it has found no impact on data integrity. Mandiant describes the attackers as advanced and suspected state-sponsored, names no group, and reports dozens of victim organizations; Arctic Wolf counts at least 78, and researcher Kevin Beaumont tracked more than 100. Responders found web shells, a rogue superuser account and stolen appliance configurations, and Mandiant warns that upgrading alone will not remove that access. The victim sectors Mandiant names are government, education, technology, financial services, telecom, and legal and professional services; food and agriculture is not among them. Editorial assessment: food and beverage plants commonly let integrators, co-packers and equipment vendors reach line controllers, refrigeration monitoring and batch systems through gateways like these, so a compromised appliance can be the first hop into production networks. - CISA alert and KEV listings (primary); Citrix bulletins CTX697096 and CTX697174; Mandiant, watchTowr, Arctic Wolf, The Hacker News, SecurityWeek - First two flaws patched and KEV-listed 27 Sep 2026; third flaw patched and KEV-listed 4 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco Talos: crimeware, Sandworm-overlapping and Qilin-deploying clusters all exploited Secure Firewall Management Center
item.category: Active exploitation — Firewall management platform, CVE-2026-20079 in CISA KEV
item.description: Talos reported on 9 September, updating on 21 September, that Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center is under active exploitation through CVE-2026-20079 (authentication bypass to root, CVSS 10.0) and CVE-2026-20316 (static credential, CVSS 5.3). It tracks three clusters: UAT-12197, crimeware using CVE-2026-20079 for web shells and credential theft; UAT-11823, which used both flaws to deploy Cyclops Blink and which Talos says overlaps in tooling with the Sandworm APT; and UAT-11988, a ransomware operator that used CVE-2026-20316 and deployed Qilin after living-off-the-land reconnaissance. Cisco released hotfixes for both flaws, with a fuller hardening release scheduled for mid-September. CISA added CVE-2026-20079 to KEV on 9 September; we did not verify a KEV listing for CVE-2026-20316. Editorial assessment: Qilin is the most active group against food and agriculture in the sector’s own data, and the management console holds the segmentation policy between IT and plant networks. - Cisco Talos (primary); BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek - Published 9 Sep 2026; Talos update 21 Sep 2026; KEV listing 9 Sep 2026

item.title: [Low] Ukraine’s largest grocery chain, ATB, confirms a cyberattack; a data-theft claim by DataSuckers is disputed
item.category: Incident — Grocery retail, IT-side (website and online services); no OT impact reported
item.description: ATB, which runs more than 1,300 stores, confirmed on 5 October that it had been hit by a cyberattack and took some online services offline, describing the website disruption as technical maintenance. It said a temporary message shown on its website did not affect the security of customer data and that the site remains fully under its control. A group calling itself DataSuckers claims to hold 7.9 million customer records, employee passport data and more than 11 million order records, has demanded $400,000, and says it will sell the data rather than leak it; ATB denies that customer data was compromised, and the claim has not been independently verified. The reporting describes no disruption to stores, logistics or payments, and no operational-technology impact has been reported. Carried as the only confirmed attack on a food-supply-chain business found this week; it is IT-side and retail. - ATB statements, as reported by The Record; DataSuckers’ claim (unverified) - Reported 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] NCC Group: August ransomware hit a 2026 high of 1,073 attacks, with industrials at 31% and Qilin leading
item.description: NCC Group’s review of August, reported by Industrial Cyber on 28 September, counted 1,073 ransomware attacks from leak-site postings, up 12% from July’s 960 and the highest monthly total this year. Industrial organizations took 329 attacks (31%), North America 473 (44%), and Qilin led all groups with 164 attacks (15%), passing The Gentlemen. The public breakdown does not isolate food and agriculture, so treat the figures as backdrop rather than a sector count; the Food and Ag-ISAC’s own data below is the better yardstick. Editorial assessment: Qilin also tops the ISAC’s sector list, which makes its behavior the most useful thing to detect against. - NCC Group, Cyber Threat Intelligence Reports: Review of August 2026 (primary data), via Industrial Cyber - Published 28 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Microsoft: one ransomware affiliate rotates Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT, and lists food and agriculture among victim sectors
item.category: Threat actor profile — Cross-sector ransomware affiliate (IT-side)
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a Storm-2570 profile on 24 September describing one affiliate that deployed four ransomware families — Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT — with largely the same toolkit: remote-management tools (MeshAgent, Atera, ScreenConnect, Splashtop, NinjaRMM), PsExec, Impacket and NetExec for lateral movement, Mimikatz-style credential theft, and s5cmd and Rclone for exfiltration. Microsoft lists food and agriculture among the affected sectors. Its recommended controls include tamper protection, attack surface reduction rules blocking PsExec and WMI lateral movement, MFA on approved remote-management tools, and credential resets if unauthorized installs appear. Anubis is also the brand that claimed July’s Fairlife attack; no link between the two is asserted. - Microsoft Threat Intelligence (primary) - Published 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Food and Ag-ISAC: sector ransomware up 62% through July; federal agencies confirmed attacks on exposed processing and grain-handling PLCs
item.category: Research — Food and Ag-ISAC sector baseline
item.description: The Food and Ag-ISAC’s State of the Threat report (3 September) counted 227 ransomware incidents against the sector through July versus 140 a year earlier (+62%), led by Qilin (47), The Gentlemen (31) and Akira (14). It says federal agencies have confirmed attacks on internet-exposed PLCs used in processing lines and grain handling, and describes Iran as blurring state operations and hacktivism while willing to target food security. Other themes: AI shortening the gap between disclosure and exploitation, nation-state positioning in OT, hacktivist escalation, and ClickFix social engineering (up 108% in the first half). In an 8 September Industrial Cyber feature, the ISAC’s Jonathan Braley said 247 incidents had been tracked through August, none resulting in food supply contamination. Editorial note: the public federal Iran-affiliated PLC advisory coverage we reviewed names water, energy and government facilities, so the food and grain-handling detail rests on the ISAC’s report. - Food and Ag-ISAC, State of the Threat: Food and Agriculture Sector Cyber Trends (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber - Report 3 Sep 2026; Industrial Cyber feature 8 Sep 2026; data through Jul–Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Nozomi: the Cling botnet hides its command traffic in STUN requests and spreads through old router, camera and DVR flaws
item.category: Research — IoT and edge-device botnet (Nozomi Networks Labs); no OT impact reported
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs reported on 1 October that a botnet it calls Cling infects routers, access points, repeaters, DVRs and cameras, mainly through CVE-2021-35394 in the Realtek Jungle SDK, and carries exploits for seven other flaws, including CVE-2014-8361, CVE-2023-26801 and CVE-2024-3721. Infected devices contact public STUN servers, and the operators send commands encoded in STUN transaction IDs while spoofing source addresses so the traffic appears to come from Google’s STUN service. Nozomi saw the bots used for denial-of-service attacks on an internet provider, a university computing cluster and game servers; it gives no victim count and reports no OT or ICS compromise. Its advice is to patch the listed flaws, restrict inbound access and watch for unusual STUN patterns. Editorial assessment: low-cost routers, DVRs and cameras are common at farms, packhouses, grain sites and cold-storage warehouses, often on the same flat network as refrigeration or irrigation controllers. - Nozomi Networks Labs (primary); The Hacker News, Industrial Cyber - Published 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Fortinet FortiMail and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-days are exploited in the wild; CISA lists both in KEV
item.category: Active exploitation — Email gateway and SD-WAN management, both in CISA KEV
item.description: Fortinet disclosed on 1 October that FortiMail CVE-2026-104286 (CVSS 9.8), a path-traversal flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files through crafted web requests, has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA added it to KEV the same day. Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2 and tells 7.2 users to move to 7.4 or later; disabling the IBE feature and limiting webmail access to trusted networks are interim workarounds. Cisco disclosed on 30 September that Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-76504 (CVSS 9.8) lets an unauthenticated attacker bypass API authentication and act as an administrator. Cisco says its PSIRT learned of active exploitation in September and that there are no workarounds; CISA added it to KEV on 30 September. Neither vendor has named an attacker or victims. Editorial assessment: processors and distributors with many plants and warehouses often link them over SD-WAN, and the mail gateway is a common starting point for phishing that ends in ransomware. - Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-175 and Cisco advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU (primary); CISA KEV; SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer - Cisco advisory 30 Sep 2026 (revised 2 Oct); Fortinet advisory 1 Oct 2026, fixed releases listed 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] IO-Link masters from three vendors share about 20 flaws, two rated CVSS 9.8; Nozomi details the attack chain
item.category: Advisory — Field-I/O firmware, about 20 CVEs, no known exploitation
item.description: CERT@VDE published three advisories on 16 September — VDE-2026-014 (Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3), VDE-2026-027 (Phoenix Contact IOL MA8) and VDE-2026-028 (Carlo Gavazzi YL212/YN115) — covering the same firmware family (versions below 1.7.4) and roughly 20 CVEs each, including two rated CVSS 9.8: an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-27546) and a malicious file upload leading to root code execution (CVE-2026-27565); ten more score 8.8. On 24 September Nozomi Networks Labs published a write-up of the Pepperl+Fuchs master, showing that chained together the flaws give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device. All three vendors point to firmware 1.7.8. No exploitation has been reported. Editorial assessment: IO-Link masters sit at the sensor and actuator layer of packaging, filling and dosing lines. - CERT@VDE advisories VDE-2026-014, -027 and -028 (primary); Nozomi Networks Labs - Advisories 16 Sep 2026; Nozomi analysis 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CERT@VDE: a CVSS 9.8 flaw in the BACnet stack of WAGO controllers, plus CODESYS runtime fixes for WAGO and other PLCs
item.category: Advisory — WAGO controllers and CODESYS runtime (CERT@VDE), no known exploitation
item.description: CERT@VDE published WAGO advisory VDE-2025-102 on 1 October for CVE-2025-41753 (CVSS 9.8), a path-traversal flaw in the BACnet/IP stack: by giving BACnet File Objects names that act as file paths, an unauthenticated attacker can read or overwrite arbitrary files, which can lead to full compromise of the device. It affects 750-811x, 750-821x, 751-9x01 and 752-8303 controllers and 762-series panels on firmware below 4.8.9 (FW30). A second WAGO advisory the same day (VDE-2025-081) covers CODESYS runtime flaws in the same families that let an unauthenticated attacker crash the device (the highest, CVE-2025-41738, is CVSS 8.3), plus a manipulated project file that can run code if a user opens it; the fix is firmware 4.10.0 (FW32). On 30 September CODESYS fixed a runtime race condition, CVE-2026-79625 (CVSS 8.1, needs authenticated monitoring access), in 3.5.22.40, with Linux-based variants due in 4.23.0.0 in the fourth quarter. No exploitation is reported for any of them. Editorial assessment: WAGO controllers and CODESYS-based PLCs are common in food-processing automation, refrigeration plant control and building management, where BACnet is the usual building-systems protocol. - CERT@VDE advisories VDE-2025-102, VDE-2025-081 and VDE-2026-097 (primary) - Published 30 Sep–1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] NIST’s draft SP 800-82 Rev. 4 adds food and agriculture to its OT security guide; comments due 30 November
item.category: Policy — NIST draft OT security guide, comment period open
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Rev. 4, Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security, on 21 September. The draft broadens sector coverage to building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail and maritime, plus industrial IoT and cloud convergence. It is restructured around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, including the Govern function, and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring, detection and zero-trust architecture, with an appendix aligning to the Risk Management Framework. It is guidance, not a mandate, and comments are open through 30 November 2026. - NIST (primary) - Draft published 21 Sep 2026; comment deadline 30 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] CISA and the FBI urge critical-infrastructure operators to put ICS integrators on least privilege and monitored remote access
item.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrator access (CISA/FBI fact sheet)
item.description: CISA and the FBI released a fact sheet, dated 23 September and reported on 24 September, on the risks of working with third-party ICS integrators. It cites an FBI-analyzed intrusion at a US industrial automation firm in March–April 2025 in which foreign actors took roughly 800 files, including customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics. Recommendations: assess what data integrators hold, apply least privilege, secure and monitor remote connections, keep offline backups, write cybersecurity requirements into contracts, disconnect public-facing devices, and weigh geopolitical factors for foreign-owned providers. Coverage names power utilities and transportation as the firm’s customers; the fact sheet does not single out food and agriculture. Editorial assessment: food plants rely on integrators for line controls, batch systems and refrigeration, so the same exposure applies. - CISA and FBI fact sheet (primary); Industrial Cyber, SecurityWeek - Fact sheet dated 23 Sep 2026; reported 24 Sep 2026
